sentences.text:
This application coming on for admission this day, the court   following:
 ORDER

Both the parties have come before this Court on the ground that they have settled their dispute amicably and prays for quashment of FIR bearing Crime No.1005/2020 registered at Police Station Kolgaon, district Satna (M.P.) for offence under Sections 420 and 34 of IPC.

During pendency of the petition, both the parties have arrived at compromise and filed the same before this Court bearing I.A.No.21712/2021 application under Section 320(2) of Cr.P.C.for Mukesh Singh Parihar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33780443/
1 compromise which is not objected on behalf of respondents.

sentences.text: Complete record of the case has been sent to the Registrar (Judicial-II) of this Court for verification of the compromise and the parties were directed to appear before him.
On verification, the Registrar has certified that both the parties have entered into a compromise without any threat, inducement and coercion from either side.
The respondent being the complainant has admitted before the Registrar that she has amicably settled her dispute with the petitioner and admitted that she has voluntarily entered into compromise.
It is submitted that the matter pertains to offence registered against the petitioner under Sections 420 and 34 of IPC.
Now both the parties have amicably settled the matter and the complainant has no more grievance against the petitioner.

In the matter of B.S. Joshi vs. State of Haryana and another reported in 2003 (4) SCC 675 whereby the Apex Court has held that Section 320 of Cr.P.C. does not limit or affect inherent powers of High Court granted under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. and in cases of matrimonial disputes if the application is filed under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. for quashing criminal proceedings or FIR or complaint, the same can be quashed.

Hon'ble the Apex Court has reiterated the view in Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab and another reported in (2012) 10 SCC 303, Narinder Singh & Others v. State of Punjab and Others (2014) 6 SCC 466, Rajiv Saxena and others vs. State Signature Not(NCT Verified of Delhi)
and another (2012) 3 SCC (Cri.) 327 and Yogendra Signed by: DEVESH K SHRIVASTAVA Yadav and others vs. State of Jharkhand and another (2014) 9 SCC Signing time: 24-01-2023 16:48:51 Considering the report of the Registrar (Judicial - II), so also the fact that the dispute between the parties have been compromised and the respondent has no grievance with the petitioner, I find that the petition needs to be allowed and it is hereby allowed.
